author_or_org: Sien Reeve O. Peralta and 10 other authors

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The study says AI coding agents commonly have their performance assessed using only merge and rejection outcomes for pull requests.
claims.quote: AI coding agents increasingly submit pull requests (Agentic-PRs) to open-source repositories, yet their performance is commonly assessed using merge and rejection outcomes alone.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The analysis examined 11,048 closed agentic pull requests, refined to 9,799 human-reviewed PRs, and manually inspected 717 representative cases.
claims.quote: To test this, we conducted a decision-oriented analysis of 11,048 closed Agentic Pull Requests, refined to 9,799 human-reviewed PRs, and manually inspected 717 representative cases to recover decision rationale from interaction artifacts.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Rejection outcomes overstate agent error: only 35.7% of rejected PRs reflected clear agentic failures, while 31.2% were driven by workflow constraints and 33.1% lacked observable decision rationale.
claims.quote: We found that rejection outcomes substantially overstate agent error: only 35.7% of rejected PRs reflected clear agentic failures, while 31.2% were driven by workflow constraints and 33.1% lacked observable decision rationale.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Among merged PRs, 15.4% required explicit reviewer involvement through feedback or direct commits, and 5.5% showed no visible interaction trace.
claims.quote: Among merged PRs, 15.4% required explicit reviewer involvement through feedback or direct commits, and 5.5% showed no visible interaction trace.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The study observed systematic differences across agents: Copilot and Devin were more often embedded in reviewer-mediated workflows, while Codex and Cursor PRs were typically merged with minimal interaction.
claims.quote: We further observed systematic differences across agents, with Copilot and Devin more often embedded in reviewer-mediated workflows, while Codex and Cursor PRs were typically merged with minimal interaction.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The authors reject PR outcomes alone as a measure of agent performance and call for interaction-aware evaluation grounded in review behavior.
claims.quote: These results reject the assumption that PR outcomes alone capture agent performance and demonstrate the need for interaction-aware evaluation grounded in review behavior.
